description: Per standings row, use the stored season-to-date win count.

a.request: For each circuit country, take the driver standings at each race held there and average the drivers' season-to-date win counts (`driverStandings.wins` as stored) within each race, then average those per-race figures across the country's races so each race counts equally (ignoring missing values). Treat the simple mean of these country figures (each country counted once) as the overall benchmark and keep the countries strictly above it. Then take the mean figure of those kept countries and keep only the ones strictly above that second mean. For each remaining country, return the country, its average, how far it is above the overall benchmark, and how far it is above the second mean, without rounding.
a.sql:
WITH race_averages AS (
  SELECT c.country, r.raceId, AVG(ds.wins) AS avg_wins
  FROM races AS r
  JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  JOIN driverStandings AS ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  WHERE c.country IS NOT NULL AND ds.wins IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.country, r.raceId
), country_averages AS (
  SELECT country, AVG(avg_wins) AS average_wins
  FROM race_averages
  GROUP BY country
), benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_wins) AS overall_benchmark
  FROM country_averages
), first_kept AS (
  SELECT ca.country, ca.average_wins, b.overall_benchmark
  FROM country_averages AS ca
  CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b
  WHERE ca.average_wins > b.overall_benchmark
), second_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_wins) AS mean_kept
  FROM first_kept
)
SELECT fk.country,
       fk.average_wins,
       fk.average_wins - fk.overall_benchmark AS above_overall_benchmark,
       fk.average_wins - sm.mean_kept AS above_second_mean
FROM first_kept AS fk
CROSS JOIN second_mean AS sm
WHERE fk.average_wins > sm.mean_kept;

b.request: For each circuit country, average the season-to-date wins from driver standings rows at each race held there, then average those race-level averages across that country's races; select countries whose averages exceed the unweighted average across all countries, then among those select countries whose averages exceed the unweighted average of that above-overall-average group, and report each selected country, its average wins, its difference above the overall average, and its difference above the group average
b.sql:
WITH race_averages AS (
  SELECT c.country, r.raceId, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_avg_wins
  FROM races AS r
  JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  JOIN driverStandings AS ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY c.country, r.raceId
), country_averages AS (
  SELECT country, AVG(race_avg_wins) AS avg_wins
  FROM race_averages
  GROUP BY country
), above_overall AS (
  SELECT country, avg_wins
  FROM country_averages
  WHERE avg_wins > (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM country_averages)
), group_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS avg_wins FROM above_overall
)
SELECT a.country,
       a.avg_wins,
       a.avg_wins - (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM country_averages) AS difference_above_overall_average,
       a.avg_wins - g.avg_wins AS difference_above_group_average
FROM above_overall AS a
CROSS JOIN group_average AS g
WHERE a.avg_wins > g.avg_wins
ORDER BY a.country;

c.request: For each circuit country, average the drivers' wins in the standings at each race held there, then average those race figures across the country's races. Which countries are above the average across countries? Among those, which are also above the average of that above-average group? For each, give the country, its average wins, how far it is above the overall average, and how far it is above the group average. Per standings row, use the stored season-to-date win count.
c.sql:
WITH race_averages AS (
  SELECT c.country, r.raceId, AVG(ds.wins) AS average_wins
  FROM races AS r
  JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
  JOIN driverStandings AS ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY c.country, r.raceId
), country_averages AS (
  SELECT country, AVG(average_wins) AS average_wins
  FROM race_averages
  GROUP BY country
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_wins) AS overall_average
  FROM country_averages
), above_overall AS (
  SELECT ca.country, ca.average_wins, o.overall_average
  FROM country_averages AS ca
  CROSS JOIN overall AS o
  WHERE ca.average_wins > o.overall_average
), group_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(average_wins) AS average_wins
  FROM above_overall
)
SELECT a.country,
       a.average_wins,
       a.average_wins - a.overall_average AS above_overall_average,
       a.average_wins - g.average_wins AS above_group_average
FROM above_overall AS a
CROSS JOIN group_average AS g
WHERE a.average_wins > g.average_wins
ORDER BY a.country;

d.request: For each country where a circuit hosted a race, calculate the average season-to-date wins recorded in the standings rows for drivers at each race, then average those race figures for the country. Which countries’ averages exceed the average across all countries? Among those countries, which also exceed the average for that above-average group? For each country in that second set, report its average wins, its difference above the overall country average, and its difference above the above-average group’s average.
d.sql:
WITH race_averages AS (
  SELECT c.country, r.raceId,
         AVG(ds.wins * 1.0) AS avg_wins
  FROM circuits c
  JOIN races r ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
  JOIN driverStandings ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY c.country, r.raceId
), country_averages AS (
  SELECT country, AVG(avg_wins) AS avg_wins
  FROM race_averages
  GROUP BY country
), above_overall AS (
  SELECT country, avg_wins
  FROM country_averages
  WHERE avg_wins > (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM country_averages)
), group_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS avg_wins
  FROM above_overall
)
SELECT a.country,
       a.avg_wins,
       a.avg_wins - (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) FROM country_averages) AS difference_above_overall_average,
       a.avg_wins - g.avg_wins AS difference_above_above_average_group_average
FROM above_overall a
CROSS JOIN group_average g
WHERE a.avg_wins > g.avg_wins
ORDER BY a.country;
